text: Rixafil is a strong inhibitor of HTX-3F.
Rixafil is given once daily by mouth.
Rixafil is dosed by body weight in patients under 50 kg.
Rixafil is excreted mainly in the faeces.
Rixafil causes mild headache in about 8% of patients.
Sevafil requires HTX-2C to form its active metabolite.
Sevafil is approved for use in adults only.
Sevafil is taken with food to reduce nausea.
Sevafil is excreted mainly in the faeces.
Sevafil is stored below 25 degrees Celsius.

Rixafil is described as a strong inhibitor of HTX-3F, which could raise exposure of any co-administered drug cleared by that enzyme. However, the information provided for Sevafil is empty: I have no data on how Sevafil is metabolised, whether it is a substrate of HTX-3F, or any other disposition pathway. Without knowing Sevafil's metabolic route, I cannot establish that Rixafil's HTX-3F inhibition affects it. Rixafil's other properties (faecal excretion, once-daily dosing, headache adverse effect) do not bear on a pharmacokinetic interaction. Therefore the available information is not sufficient to confirm an interaction; no mechanism linking the two drugs can be identified from what I hold.
